newsitem.title: USA: US clears Yugoslavia, Turkey air standards.
newsitem.headline: US clears Yugoslavia, Turkey air standards.

text.p: U.S. aviation officials on Monday rated Yugoslavia and Turkey as in compliance with international air safety standards but gave Thailand and the Ivory Coast only conditional approval.
Turkey was raised in the assessment by the Federal Aviation Administration to full compliance from conditional. The ratings for the other three were their first.

The FAA said the assessments do not indicate whether individual foreign airlines were safe or unsafe, but whether the countries had civil aviation authorities and the extent to which those authorities ensured safe airline operations.
It said the Category I rating for Yugoslavia and Turkey meant their aviation authorities complied with International Civil Aviation Organization safety standards.

The Category II conditional rating for Thailand and the Ivory Coast meant their authorities did not meet the ICAO standards, but the FAA was negotiating with them to correct their deficiencies, the FAA said.
During the negotiations, it said, limited operations by its airlines to the United States was permitted under heightened FAA surveillance.
A Category III noncompliance rating means a country fails to meet ICAO standards and has no aviation authority to assure the safety of airline operations, the FAA said.

Operations to the United States by a carrier from a Category III country are not allowed unless the country arranges to have its flights conducted by an airline certified by a country that meets international safety standards.
The FAA said it only assesses countries whose airlines have operating rights to or from the United States or have requested such rights.
